summary: Firebase Email/Password provider is now ENABLED — signUp and signInWithPassword both return HTTP 200. However, real end-to-end persistence is only PARTIAL. Direct REST probes of Firestore prove: (a) 'tyres' collection contains the MRF FBV1-Test doc `HaCnlPSQMO5So8Im43pU` (20-char Firestore id) → tyre write succeeded; (b) 'settings/shop' doc exists → shop save succeeded and persists after page.reload(); (c) 'users' collection is EMPTY → AuthContext is NOT upserting user profile on signup; (d) 'sales' collection is EMPTY → sale save silently fails; (e) 'customers' collection is EMPTY → customer upsert silently fails. Root cause of the UI-side failures: the tyres list query `where('categoryId','==',x) + orderBy('brand')` requires a Firestore composite index that has not been deployed; console shows 'FirebaseError: The query requires an index. You can create it here: https://console.firebase.google.com/v1/r/project/tyrebook-dea3f/firestore/indexes?create_composite=...'. Because the sale-save code path (sales/new → save & reduce stock) reads the tyres list to locate the SKU for stock decrement, that read throws first and the sale + customer upsert never get committed — so writes for those two never happen. No PERMISSION_DENIED / rules issues; Firestore rules are permissive.

integration_issues.flow: Firebase Auth ↔ AuthContext user profile upsert
integration_issues.issue: After successful accounts:signUp (HTTP 200), the app does NOT create a corresponding document in the Firestore 'users' collection. REST probe on /projects/tyrebook-dea3f/databases/(default)/documents/users returned `{}` (empty). Expect AuthContext (src/firebase/auth.ts / src/context/AuthContext.tsx or equivalent) to setDoc(users/{uid}) with role, displayName, email, createdAt on signUp/first-login. Currently missing — role/permissions are stored only in localStorage under tyrebook.role, which does not survive cross-device access.

listTyres in src/firebase/inventory.ts:41-59 runs `query(col, where('categoryId','==', x), orderBy('brand'))` which requires a composite index. The console prints: 'FirebaseError: The query requires an index. You can create it here: https://console.firebase.google.com/v1/r/project/tyrebook-dea3f/firestore/indexes?create_composite=Ckxwcm9qZWN0cy90eXJlYm9vay1kZWEzZi9kYXRhYmFzZXMvKGRlZmF1bHQpL2NvbGxlY3Rpb25Hcm91cHMvdHlyZXMvaW5kZXhlcy9fEAEaDgoKY2F0ZWdvcnlJZBABGgkKBWJyYW5kEAEaDAoIX19uYW1lX18QAQ'. The error is swallowed by `console.warn` + `setItems([])` in app/inventory/[category].tsx:38, so the user sees a permanently empty list even after a successful write. Fix options: (a) deploy the composite index via Firebase Console link or `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` with a firestore.indexes.json; (b) drop the orderBy and sort client-side; (c) surface the error to the UI instead of silent empty state.

After tapping sale-save-btn with a valid payload (GST, MRF FBV1-Test, qty 1, ₹1500, 18% GST, Cash) the URL stays on /sales/new (no redirect to /(tabs)/billing) and REST probe of 'sales' collection returns `{}` — no doc was created. The 2 Write/channel POSTs observed on the wire are Firebase's persistent RPC channel setup, not actual doc commits. RCA: the create-sale flow first calls listTyres()/getStock() to reduce inventory; that read throws the composite-index error above, so addDoc(sales/*) never fires. Same cascade breaks 'customers' upsert. Fix requires the tyres index (see above) OR reworking sale save to not depend on the failing query.

Sale save failure is completely silent — no toast, no red inline error, no console.error. User believes the sale was recorded. Recommend surfacing thrown errors from sales.ts / stock.ts to the sale-save-btn handler.

Q8: after clearing tyrebook.* localStorage and reloading, Firebase Auth persistence (IndexedDB firebaseLocalStorageDb) keeps the user signed in — /login is skipped. Navigating to /inventory/car still shows 'No tyres yet' although REST proves the MRF FBV1-Test doc lives in Firestore. Same root cause: missing composite index blocks the read.

action_items: USER/DEV ACTION (highest priority): Deploy the missing Firestore composite index for the tyres collection. Fastest path — open the URL from the console warning: https://console.firebase.google.com/v1/r/project/tyrebook-dea3f/firestore/indexes?create_composite=Ckxwcm9qZWN0cy90eXJlYm9vay1kZWEzZi9kYXRhYmFzZXMvKGRlZmF1bHQpL2NvbGxlY3Rpb25Hcm91cHMvdHlyZXMvaW5kZXhlcy9fEAEaDgoKY2F0ZWdvcnlJZBABGgkKBWJyYW5kEAEaDAoIX19uYW1lX18QAQ and click 'Create index'. Fields: categoryId ASC, brand ASC. Or add /app/frontend/firestore.indexes.json with the same composite and deploy via Firebase CLI. This single change should unblock Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8.

MAIN AGENT (E1) code change: In src/firebase/inventory.ts, drop the composite `orderBy('brand')` and sort client-side (list.sort((a,b)=>a.brand.localeCompare(b.brand))) so no index is needed. This is a one-line change and makes the app resilient to missing indexes. Also do the same review in src/firebase/sales.ts / customers / khata / purchase in case similar where+orderBy queries exist there.

MAIN AGENT (E1): AuthContext must upsert users/{uid} on signUp. Confirm src/context/AuthContext.tsx (or wherever signUp is consumed) calls setDoc(users/<uid>, { role, displayName, email, createdAt: serverTimestamp() }, { merge: true }). Currently the 'users' Firestore collection stays empty after signup.
MAIN AGENT (E1): Bubble up sales.ts / stock.ts errors to the /sales/new UI. Right now a save-failure produces no toast and the user cannot tell the sale was rejected.

TESTING AGENT (next iteration): After the composite index is created, re-run V4–V8 — expect a tyre row in /inventory/car (testID `tyre-HaCnl…`), a sale doc in the 'sales' collection, a 'Firebase Test' row in /customers, and cross-session persistence to hold after localStorage wipe.
critical_code_review_comments: src/firebase/inventory.ts:53-59 — `query(col, where('categoryId','==',x), orderBy('brand'))` requires a composite index. Either declare the index (firestore.indexes.json) or drop the orderBy and sort in JS.
app/inventory/[category].tsx:34-40 — catches the Firestore index error with `console.warn` + `setItems([])`; the user has no way to know reads are broken. Please propagate as an inline error banner.

AuthContext / src/firebase/auth.ts:78+ (signUp) — the flow does not appear to write a users/{uid} document; the 'users' collection is empty after two successful signup attempts. This means role (owner vs staff) is not portable across devices.

src/firebase/sales.ts (create sale) — the sale-save path clearly depends on the tyres read (to reduce stock). Any exception from that read aborts the entire transaction with no user feedback. Guard the stock lookup or catch + still create the sale.

success_rate.frontend: Auth 100% (Q1,Q3). Writes: Shop ✓ Tyre ✓, User profile ✗, Sale ✗, Customer ✗. Reads: Shop ✓, Tyre ✗ (index), Sale ✗, Customer ✗.

seed_data_creation: Firebase Auth: created user owner@test.com (UID assigned by Firebase). Firestore docs left in place as proof: tyres/HaCnlPSQMO5So8Im43pU (MRF FBV1-Test) and settings/shop (Shop Name = 'Firebase Verified Shop').
context_for_next_testing_agent: The blocker is the Firestore composite index on tyres (categoryId ASC, brand ASC). Either create it via the console link in the RCA, or ship a code fix that drops orderBy from listTyres. Once done, re-run: /inventory/car should show `tyre-HaCnlPSQMO5So8Im43pU` (already in DB); a new /sales/new save should populate the 'sales' and 'customers' collections; /customers should list 'Firebase Test'. Also validate that AuthContext writes users/{uid} on signup (a fresh signup, e.g. 'staff2@test.com', should create a doc under 'users' — currently it does not).
rca_of_issue: REPRODUCTION: (1) Login as owner@test.com / Password@123 — signInWithPassword returns 200 ✓. (2) Go /inventory/car → tap +, fill Brand=MRF, Model=FBV1-Test, Size=185/65 R15, Purchase=1000, Selling=1500, Stock=5, Rack=A1, Save. Network shows 3× POST to firestore.googleapis.com/google.firestore.v1.Firestore/Write/channel. (3) Return to /inventory/car → screen shows 'No tyres yet'. (4) Console: 'FirebaseError: The query requires an index. You can create it here: https://console.firebase.google.com/v1/r/project/tyrebook-dea3f/firestore/indexes?create_composite=Ckxwcm9qZWN0cy90eXJlYm9vay1kZWEzZi9kYXRhYmFzZXMvKGRlZmF1bHQpL2NvbGxlY3Rpb25Hcm91cHMvdHlyZXMvaW5kZXhlcy9fEAEaDgoKY2F0ZWdvcnlJZBABGgkKBWJyYW5kEAEaDAoIX19uYW1lX18QAQ'. (5) REST GET https://firestore.googleapis.com/v1/projects/tyrebook-dea3f/databases/(default)/documents/tyres?key=... → HTTP 200 with document id `HaCnlPSQMO5So8Im43pU` (Firestore-style 20-char alphanumeric — NOT a `local-` id), proving the WRITE succeeded but the READ query is failing. (6) /sales/new save + /admin/shop save: same Write/channel POSTs, but REST GET sales and customers return `{}`. REST GET settings returns the shop doc. So the sale/customer writes silently roll back — root cause is that sale-save internally calls listTyres to reduce stock, throwing the same composite-index error before addDoc(sales/*) runs. MITIGATION: create the composite index (link above) OR drop `orderBy('brand')` from listTyres and sort client-side.

evidence.Q1_signup_signin_200: YES — POST accounts:signUp -> 200 (first script) and POST accounts:signInWithPassword -> 200 (login script). accounts:lookup + accounts:update also 200.
evidence.Q2_user_profile_written_to_firestore: NO — REST GET https://firestore.googleapis.com/v1/projects/tyrebook-dea3f/databases/(default)/documents/users?key=... returns `{}` after 2 successful signups. AuthContext is not upserting users/{uid}.
evidence.Q4_inventory: PARTIAL — WRITE observed (POST Write/channel × 3) AND doc really exists in Firestore: id `HaCnlPSQMO5So8Im43pU` (20 chars, alphanumeric, not `local-…`). READ fails because of missing composite index → UI stays empty ('No tyres yet').
evidence.Q5_sales: NO — Write/channel POSTs observed on the wire but the 'sales' collection is `{}` per REST probe. Save did NOT redirect to /(tabs)/billing; URL stayed at /sales/new. Root cause: sale-save internally reads tyres and throws the index error.
evidence.Q6_customer: NO — 'customers' collection is `{}` per REST probe. /customers screen shows 'No customers yet'. Same chained failure as Q5.
evidence.Q7_settings: YES — 3 Write/channel POSTs during Save Changes; REST GET settings/shop shows the full doc; page.reload() shows 'Firebase Verified Shop' in the shop-name field. This flow uses setDoc(settings/shop) which needs no index — that's why it works and the others don't.
evidence.Q8_cross_session_persistence: PARTIAL — data IS in Firestore (tyre doc `HaCnlPSQMO5So8Im43pU`) but /inventory/car still shows 'No tyres yet' after localStorage wipe + auto-relogin, again due to the missing composite index. Also observed: clearing `tyrebook.*` from localStorage does NOT log the user out because Firebase persists auth in IndexedDB (firebaseLocalStorageDb) — so re-login step in the flow was skipped by the app.
evidence.Q9_permission_or_auth_errors: NO PERMISSION_DENIED. NO 'Missing or insufficient permissions'. One repeated FirebaseError: 'The query requires an index' from listTyres.

doc_id_prefixes.tyre_HaCnl_len20: HaCnl (full id HaCnlPSQMO5So8Im43pU, 20-char alphanumeric — REAL Firestore id, NOT local-…)
doc_id_prefixes.sale: N/A — no sale doc was actually created in Firestore
doc_id_prefixes.customer: N/A — no customer doc was actually created in Firestore
doc_id_prefixes.settings_shop: shop (document id is the literal string 'shop', per setDoc(settings/shop) — expected)

evidence.auth_failures: None on this run. All identitytoolkit responses were HTTP 200.

verdict: PARTIAL — Firebase Auth is fully active and Firestore accepts writes (tyre and shop docs are truly persisted in Firestore, verified by REST probe). BUT: (a) missing composite index on `tyres (categoryId,brand)` breaks all inventory reads and cascades into sale/customer save failures; (b) AuthContext does not upsert users/{uid} on signup. Fix the composite index (link in RCA) + add users write, then Firebase will be FULLY ACTIVE.
